description: Global energy and SDG7 indicators from IEA and UN publications. Estimates, scenarios and historical observations are kept distinct.

records.method: IEA Global Energy Review 2026 estimate using energy balance data
records.caveat: Demand growth rate, not absolute energy consumption and not an efficiency metric.

records.indicator: Solar PV contribution to growth in global energy demand
records.method: IEA decomposition of incremental energy demand by source
records.caveat: Share of the increase in demand, not share of total energy supply or electricity generation.

records.indicator: Low-emissions sources contribution to growth in global energy demand
records.method: IEA decomposition; low-emissions group includes solar, wind, nuclear, hydropower and other renewables
records.caveat: Share of growth; do not compare directly with generation-mix shares.

records.indicator: Renewable share of global electricity generation
records.caveat: Renewables include solar, wind, hydropower, geothermal, bioenergy, waste and marine. Nuclear is excluded from this renewable share.

records.indicator: Low-emissions share of global electricity generation
records.caveat: Includes renewables and nuclear. Not identical to renewable-only share.
Estimated investment, not final audited spending. MER means market exchange rate.

records.indicator: Investment in renewables, nuclear, grids, storage, low-emissions fuels, efficiency and electrification
records.caveat: Combined group contains multiple supply and end-use categories; not all entries are renewable generation.

records.method: IEA estimate of change in total energy supply per unit of GDP
records.caveat: Part of the 2026 improvement is attributed to forced consumption cuts from energy supply disruption; not all is structural technical efficiency.

records.method: IEA Electricity 2026 and Energy Efficiency 2026 projections
records.caveat: Forecast, not observed final value. Drivers include industry, transport electrification, cooling and data centres.
Access does not by itself measure affordability, reliability, quality or clean generation.
Population count; do not infer equal severity of deprivation across households or regions.

records.indicator: Global population with access to clean cooking
records.caveat: Access may not capture affordability, reliability, sustained use or all exposure conditions.

records.indicator: Electricity share in total final energy consumption in IEA Stated Policies Scenario
records.method: IEA World Energy Outlook 2026 STEPS scenario
records.caveat: Scenario outcome conditional on stated policies and assumptions; not a guaranteed forecast.

interpretation_rules: Keep power (W), energy (Wh), capacity, generation, primary energy, final energy and energy services distinct.
Never equate reduced demand caused by deprivation or supply disruption with durable efficiency improvement.
Keep renewable generation shares, low-emissions generation shares and contributions to demand growth as different indicators.
An estimate or scenario is not an observed fact.
More energy access may be necessary for justice even while avoidable waste and environmental harm must be reduced.
